texts.full_text: ly is it one of the most thrilling parts of "Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea," but also an event that allows for extensive use of contrasting and diverse textures. The scene itself offers a dynamic setting—a battle in the depths, where light struggles to penetrate through the murky water. In my artwork, I aimed at capturing this sense of depth using one-point perspective with meticulous attention paid to how different elements interact within that space. To represent the ocean's vastness and its inhabitants' textures, a minimum of 10 distinct textural techniques were utilized: stippling for light diffusion in deep sea water; cross-hatching for shadows cast by both Nautilus and giant squid as they grapple with each other under dim bioluminescence; fine lines to depict the intricate details on their skin patterns—both natural camouflage against predators, but also a display of power during confrontation. The background was crEated using different shades of gray ink washes. the deeper parts are darker and more saturated in color while gradually becoming lighter as we move towards where our protagonists engage with each other; this not only adds depth to the artwork visually (a requirement for one-point perspective) but also symbolically represents how much is unknown about life deep within oceans compared to what's happening at sea level. The giant squid, though it plays a significant role in my interpretation of "Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea," was given minimal details due to its elusive nature. texts.full_text: e of the highlights was watching a performance by Beatroot Weekend. This extraordinary group consists entirely of people who are under-18 but have autistic spectrum conditions, which we felt needed to be acknowledged and celebrated. When they were on stage performing, there is an unmistakable shift in how their minds work; you can watch it unfold before your eyes as the performance takes shape – from intricate details such as a spoon clattering onto a plate or stepping backwards off of one foot. Their actions are directly connected to complex meanings and emotions. This made me realise that there is no art form which communicates meaning more clearly than behavioural dance (like Beatroot Weekend’s work). When watching their performance, I felt completely immersed in the message they were trying to communicate – even when only a few of us understood it. The world was consumed by emotion and beauty. A week after that it's last-quarter, then back to new, which completes the 29-and-a-half-day cycle. Last-quarter Moon produces some of the lowest tides. Ocean tides are produced by the gravitational pull of the Moon and Sun. When the Moon is new or full, the Moon and Sun pull along the same line, so their combined gravity produces high tides. But when the Moon’s at a quarter phase, the Sun and Moon pull at right angles to each other — partially cancelling the other’s pull.
